005package org.wpilib.util;
006
007/**
008 * Persistent alert. Alerts are tagged with a type of {@code HIGH}, {@code MEDIUM}, or {@code LOW}
009 * to denote urgency. See {@link org.wpilib.util.Alert.Level Level} for suggested usage of each
010 * type. Alerts can be displayed on supported dashboards, and are shown in a priority order based on
011 * type and recency of activation, with newly activated alerts first.
012 *
013 * <p>Alerts should be created once and stored persistently, then updated to "active" or "inactive"
014 * as necessary. {@link #set(boolean)} can be safely called periodically.
015 *
016 * <pre>
017 * class Robot {
018 *   Alert alert = new Alert("somethingWrong", "Something went wrong", Alert.Level.MEDIUM);
019 *
020 *   periodic() {
021 *     alert.set(...);
022 *   }
023 * }
024 * </pre>
025 *
026 * <p>Alternatively, alerts which are only used once at startup can be created and activated inline.
027 *
028 * <pre>
029 * public Robot() {
030 *   new Alert("autoPathsFailed", "Failed to load auto paths", Alert.Level.HIGH).set(true);
031 * }
032 * </pre>
033 */
034public class Alert implements AutoCloseable {
035  /** Represents an alert's level of urgency. */
036  public enum Level {
037    /**
038     * High priority alert - displayed first with a red "X" symbol. Use this type for problems which
039     * will seriously affect the robot's functionality and thus require immediate attention.
040     */
041    HIGH(AlertDataJNI.LEVEL_HIGH),
042
043    /**
044     * Medium priority alert - displayed second with a yellow "!" symbol. Use this type for problems
045     * which could affect the robot's functionality but do not necessarily require immediate
046     * attention.
047     */
048    MEDIUM(AlertDataJNI.LEVEL_MEDIUM),
049
050    /**
051     * Low priority alert - displayed last with a green "i" symbol. Use this type for problems which
052     * are unlikely to affect the robot's functionality, or any other alerts which do not fall under
053     * the other categories.
054     */
055    LOW(AlertDataJNI.LEVEL_LOW);
056
057    private final int m_value;
058
059    Level(int value) {
060      m_value = value;
061    }
062
063    /**
064     * Gets the integer value for this level.
065     *
066     * @return Integer value for this level.
067     */
068    public int getValue() {
069      return m_value;
070    }
071  }
072
073  private final Level m_level;
074  private int m_handle;
075
076  /**
077   * Creates a new alert in the default group - "Alerts".
078   *
079   * @param id Alert identifier. This should be unique within the group.
080   * @param text Text to be displayed when the alert is active.
081   * @param level Alert urgency level.
082   */
083  public Alert(String id, String text, Level level) {
084    this("Alerts", id, text, level);
085  }
086
087  /**
088   * Creates a new alert.
089   *
090   * @param group Group identifier.
091   * @param id Alert identifier. This should be unique within the group.
092   * @param text Text to be displayed when the alert is active.
093   * @param level Alert urgency level.
094   */
095  public Alert(String group, String id, String text, Level level) {
096    m_level = level;
097    m_handle = WPIUtilJNI.createAlert(group, id, text, level.m_value);
098  }
099
100  /**
101   * Sets whether the alert should currently be displayed. This method can be safely called
102   * periodically.
103   *
104   * @param active Whether to display the alert.
105   */
106  public void set(boolean active) {
107    WPIUtilJNI.setAlertActive(m_handle, active);
108  }
109
110  /**
111   * Gets whether the alert is active.
112   *
113   * @return whether the alert is active.
114   */
115  public boolean get() {
116    return WPIUtilJNI.isAlertActive(m_handle);
117  }
118
119  /**
120   * Updates current alert text. Use this method to dynamically change the displayed alert, such as
121   * including more details about the detected problem.
122   *
123   * @param text Text to be displayed when the alert is active.
124   */
125  public void setText(String text) {
126    WPIUtilJNI.setAlertText(m_handle, text);
127  }
128
129  /**
130   * Gets the current alert text.
131   *
132   * @return the current text.
133   */
134  public String getText() {
135    return WPIUtilJNI.getAlertText(m_handle);
136  }
137
138  /**
139   * Get the level of this alert.
140   *
141   * @return the level
142   */
143  public Level getLevel() {
144    return m_level;
145  }
146
147  @Override
148  public void close() {
149    if (m_handle != 0) {
150      WPIUtilJNI.destroyAlert(m_handle);
151      m_handle = 0;
152    }
153  }
154}
